findings.title: _sanitize_particles divides by dt without a zero-guard, crashing when time_scale=0
findings.description: At line 1439, `_sanitize_particles` computes `max_speed = max(s.cfl * g.voxel_size / dt * 2.0, 50.0)` with an unguarded division by `dt`. The companion method `_cfl_speed_limit` (line 1386) explicitly guards this case with `safe_dt = max(float(dt), 1.0e-8)`, but `_sanitize_particles` does not use that guard. When `s.time_scale = 0` (a valid user setting that pauses the simulation), `frame_dt = s.time_scale / s.frame_rate` yields 0.0; then `dt = frame_dt / substeps` is also 0.0, and this line raises `ZeroDivisionError` on the host. There is no early-return for `frame_dt == 0` in `step_frame` before `_sanitize_particles(dt)` is called at line 1752.
findings.impact: Setting time_scale to 0 crashes the solver with an unhandled ZeroDivisionError instead of pausing gracefully. This is a hard crash on the Blender main thread.
findings.fix: Either reuse `_cfl_speed_limit(dt)` to compute `max_speed` (which already has the `safe_dt` guard), or add `safe_dt = max(float(dt), 1.0e-8)` before the division: `max_speed = max(s.cfl * g.voxel_size / safe_dt * 2.0, 50.0)`. Additionally, consider an early-return in `step_frame` when `frame_dt <= 0`.

findings.title: solve_jacobi_st hardcodes last_residual = -1.0, hiding divergence diagnostics
findings.description: At lines 1827-1828, `solve_jacobi_st` sets `self.last_residual = -1.0` and `self.last_residual_squared = -1.0` after running a fixed iteration budget, then unconditionally reports `PRESSURE_STATUS_JACOBI` with `pressure_valid=True`. The non-ST variant `solve_jacobi` (lines 2001-2012) was explicitly fixed to compute the real residual via `self.measure_residual(voxel_type)`, and its comment states: 'the previous hardcoded last_residual = -1.0 actively hid whether that fixed budget was actually enough: diagnostics/UI/validation could not distinguish a well-converged Jacobi solve from a wildly divergent one.' The ST variant was never given the same fix. `_set_pressure_status` (line 1691) uses `self.last_residual` to build the status dict, so `_pressure` in solver.py stores a negative residual into `self.stats.pressure_residual`.
findings.impact: In spacetime mode, the UI/diagnostics show a meaningless -1.0 residual for ST Jacobi solves. A wildly divergent pressure field is indistinguishable from a converged one, and the solver always projects it (pressure_valid=True). This can mask numerical instability in ST-FLIP simulations.
findings.fix: Port the residual computation from `solve_jacobi` into `solve_jacobi_st`: replace lines 1827-1828 with `residual = self.measure_residual(voxel_type); self.last_residual = residual if math.isfinite(residual) else math.inf; self.last_residual_squared = (residual * residual if math.isfinite(residual) else math.inf)`.

findings.title: k_sanitize_mac_velocity does not sanitize NaN/Inf in face weight arrays
findings.description: In `k_sanitize_mac_velocity` (lines 252-298), when a velocity value is NaN or Inf, the kernel zeroes the velocity (`u[tid] = 0.0`) and then reduces the weight only if `wu[tid] > 1.0e-8`. If `wu[tid]` is itself NaN, the comparison `wu[tid] > 1.0e-8` evaluates to False (NaN comparisons always return False), so the NaN weight is left unchanged. Similarly, if only the weight is NaN but the velocity is finite and large, the `elif wu[tid] > 1.0e-8` branch is skipped and the velocity is neither clamped nor the weight fixed. A NaN face weight poisons the MAC normalization kernel (`k_normalize_mac`) in the next substep, which divides by weight sums.
findings.impact: A single NaN face weight persists through sanitization and propagates NaN into the MAC velocity field on the next P2G/normalize cycle, potentially destabilizing the simulation after a pressure-projection blowup that the sanitize step was designed to contain.
findings.fix: Add explicit NaN/Inf checks for the weight arrays in the kernel. When `wu[tid]` is NaN or Inf, set it to 0.0 (or a small epsilon). Apply the same check to `wv[tid]` and `ww[tid]`.

findings.title: PCG conditional-graph cache uses blind full eviction instead of LRU
findings.description: At line 1559, `_get_pcg_conditional_graphs` checks `if len(self._pcg_conditional_graphs) >= 8: self._pcg_conditional_graphs.clear()`. This evicts ALL cached CUDA graphs when the cache reaches 8 entries, rather than evicting the least-recently-used entry. If the solver alternates between different `(work_n, batch, max_iterations, tol_sq)` keys (e.g., due to adaptive topology or user parameter changes), every capacity crossing forces re-capturing all graphs, each requiring a `wp.synchronize_device` call (line 1561). An OrderedDict with `popitem(last=False)` would evict one entry per miss.
findings.impact: Repeated CUDA graph re-captures during normal operation when the active working set slightly exceeds 8 variants. This causes GPU stalls from the synchronize + capture cycle, degrading pressure-solve throughput.
findings.fix: Use `collections.OrderedDict` (already imported at line 33). On cache miss when at capacity, call `self._pcg_conditional_graphs.popitem(last=False)` to evict only the oldest entry. Move accessed entries to the end on cache hit with `move_to_end(key)`.

findings.title: Native PCG graph-capture failure silently degrades to host-batched with no diagnostic surface
findings.description: At lines 2099-2105, when `_get_pcg_conditional_graphs` throws during CUDA graph capture, the exception is caught and stored in `self.last_pcg_native_error`, and `self._pcg_native_available` is permanently set to `False`. The solver then silently falls back to the host-batched PCG loop. No warning, log, or event is emitted to the UI or profiler. The user sees a significant performance drop (host-batched mode requires per-batch host readbacks) with no indication of why. The `last_pcg_native_error` string is only accessible programmatically; nothing in `step_frame` or `_pressure` checks or surfaces it.
findings.impact: A transient CUDA driver error during graph capture permanently disables the native path and causes silent, ongoing performance degradation. Users cannot diagnose the cause without inspecting internal solver state.
findings.fix: After the except block, emit a warning via the profiler or a solver stats flag (e.g., `self.stats.pcg_native_degraded = True`) that the UI/diagnostics panel can surface. Consider logging the error message once rather than silently storing it.
